summary: Partial tenant diversion to legacy variant during staged prefetch causes tokenization divergence and elevated error rate
description:
Issue summary:
During a staged canary prefetch for redwood-chat-7b-v1 we observed a subset of Cartwheel tenant traffic being silently routed to the legacy tokenization variant (redwood-chat-7b-v1-legacy-tokenizer). The divergence was not visible at routing policy configuration (no explicit pin change) and manifested as mixed-quality outputs, higher 5xx spike rate, and user-reported hallucination/formatting regressions.

Impact:
- ~6% of requests for Cartwheel (enterprise dedicated account) returned responses produced by the legacy-tokenizer variant over a 42 minute window.
- Customer reported elevated error rate (5xx) and malformed structured outputs in checkout assistant flows.
- Business impact: intermittent customer confusion and increased chatbot failures during a peak campaign window.

Environment:
- Prod - us-east-1, dedicated capacity pool dc-prod-7b-01 assigned to Cartwheel.
- Canary rollout for redwood-chat-7b-v1 (weight ramping 5% -> 25%) using prefetch/batched mirror strategy.

Important notes: routing rules in Console show model pin intact; no manual pin change recorded in audit log during the window. Edge proxies show a subset of sessions with legacy tokenizer header present (x-rt-tokenizer: legacy), but the header was not present on the original client request.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a staged prefetch canary for redwood-chat-7b-v1 with prewarm mirror enabled.
2) Target a dedicated tenant (Cartwheel) with session affinity enabled and model pin to redwood-chat-7b-v1.
3) Trigger bulk prefetch traffic via load test or real traffic ramp.
4) Observe edge logs for x-rt-tokenizer header and compare model hash returned from orchestrator.
5) Correlate timestamps with serving runtime traces and KV-cache keys for the tenant session.
observed_behavior: Intermittent routing of some requests to redwood-chat-7b-v1-legacy-tokenizer leading to tokenization mismatch, malformed JSON outputs, and a 5xx spike (~4.8% baseline -> 12.6% during window).
expected_behavior: All pinned sessions for Cartwheel should route exclusively to redwood-chat-7b-v1 during the promotion window; prefetch should mirror traffic without altering tokenizer headers or shifting live requests to legacy variants.
impact: Customer-facing regressions in checkout assistant; elevated error rate and several enterprise escalation messages to CS. Estimated affected sessions: ~9k during 42-minute window. Billing not impacted but service quality degraded.
logs_and_traces: edge-proxy logs: edge-prod-us-east-1-2026-03-13-18:12:xx - tenant=cartwheel - request_id=R-9a7c - x-rt-tokenizer: legacy
serving-runtime error: srv-7b-01 - 2026-03-13T18:18:05Z - KV cache miss -> fallback to local-legacy-instantiation - stacktrace: OOM-guard triggered during prewarm
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: prefetch path mutated request headers during mirror fanout causing edge to consider requests for legacy tokenizer variant.
Edge logs show x-rt-tokenizer header injected between mirror proxy and orchestrator for ~6% of mirrored requests. Header not present from client side.
Checked audit logs: no pin change; routing policy unchanged. Canary weight events: 5%->10% transition occurred at 18:05 UTC followed by prewarm burst at 18:06-18:20.
Replayed mirrored payloads against both tokenizer variants: legacy-tokenizer produced different token boundaries and occasional unclosed JSON blocks triggering downstream parser 5xx.
Orchestrator PR #2213 added a prefetch optimization that merges header contexts from mirror source; suspected to accidentally include upstream edge header set — flagged as potential root cause.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Escalating to SRE and Orchestrator team. Customer impacted during promotional window — they requested immediate mitigation.
Lucas Chen (SRE): Reproduced header injection in staging with canary mirror enabled. Creating hotpatch to strip tokenizer headers on mirror path. See slack #support-cartwheel thread.
Maya Ruiz (Platform Eng): Noted PR 2213 comment about copying context for prewarm - will audit header copying logic. Assigning review to Orchestrator team.
Cartwheel CS rep (Kevin Hsu): Customer confirms mixed outputs and provided two request IDs where checkout assistant returned invalid JSON.
Lucas Chen: Temporarily paused prefetch mirror for Cartwheel tenant at 2026-03-13T19:02Z UTC — error rate reverted towards baseline within 3 minutes.
Maya Ruiz: Opened github PR to strip x-rt-tokenizer and other runtime-only headers from mirror payloads: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2220
workaround: Paused prefetch/mirror for Cartwheel (applied at 2026-03-13T19:02Z). Manually enforced header sanitize rule on edge for tenant Cartwheel to drop x-rt-tokenizer header for server-to-server mirror traffic. Customer routed to full-weight pinned variant until fix is deployed.
resolution: Hotpatch applied: edge header sanitizer rule implemented (edge-proxy hotpatch 2026-03-13T19:05Z) and prefetch mirror header-copy behavior reverted. Orchestrator PR #2220 merged to ensure mirror payloads do not carry runtime-only tokenizer headers. Post-deploy monitoring shows 5xx rate returned to baseline and no further legacy-tokenizer responses observed for Cartwheel. Follow-up: permanent test added to prewarm e2e suite to validate header isolation; postmortem scheduled.
follow_up_actions: Add unit/integration tests to prewarm mirror path to assert header whitelisting
Audit other tenants with prefetch enabled for similar header leakage over last 7 days
